description:
Implement the spec in .openspec/specs/filed-order-immutability/spec.md. Pipeline for this order is sdlc-default (software domain, the factory repo itself), selected by the run workflow.

STAGING: this order is filed and staged only. The spec and this work order record sit on the branch anvil/run-filed-order-immutability, the issue carries no anvil label, and no run is fired. Execution starts on the owner's word. Run configuration baseline, unchanged by this filing: the order is parented on factory main 4675a131eb9aa88097741dc3cdc9772c3db17550 (the fixed spine merged by wo-gh-39), whose anvil.yaml carries max_run_tokens 6000000, max_runtime_turns 40 and max_packet_tokens 48000, and whose anvil.json wires the checks command (python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py').

EVIDENCE (the defect this order closes):
In the C64 blueprint chain (project c64-retro-hardware, run 43673692204), the intake station rewrote the run's copy of the filed order wo-gh-7 mid-run: risk medium became low and surfaces [ui, content, deploy] became [content]. Routing consumed the rewritten values and the reviewer panel shrank from six to two, so the approved verdict rested on a third of the designed panel, and nothing in the run record treated the rewrite as an event. In the same chain the filed spec was amended mid-run inside the .openspec/specs/ tree. The factory's own record shows the same shape: wo-gh-39 was filed with risk low and surfaces [api], and its run copy (work_orders/wo-gh-39.json) carries risk medium and surfaces [deploy, api, content]. The comparison against other software factories (factory research of 2026-11-15, report section "Mechanisms ANVIL Does Not Have", mechanisms 1 to 6 for failure mode 1 and 13 to 18 for failure mode 3) shows the equivalent enforced technically elsewhere: Attractor validates the pipeline graph before execution and no running node redefines it; the Copilot coding agent's credential can only push to copilot/* branches; ZazenCodes makes the orchestrator the only writer of the job record.

BUILD, per the spec requirements:
R1: at run start the runner snapshots the filed work order record and records its sha256 in the run report. The station tool permission layer (the layer tools/claude_station.py uses for the reviewer scoped path) denies every station any write to the filed record path and to record paths of the current work order under work-orders/ and work_orders/. A denied attempt is recorded as a named finding (station, path, operation).
R2: the runner maintains the run's effective work order in the run tree, written only by runner code. Intake delivers its outcome as its station artifact. Filed risk and surfaces win where the filing sets them; intake may stamp risk and surfaces only where the filed record leaves them null; a rescope may replace the description with the cut recorded. The effective record freezes when intake completes; after the freeze no station output, correction or loopback can change risk, surfaces, kind, spec_path or the description. A post-freeze change requires a new filing, and a run that would need one stops and records that reason.
R3: routing (anvil/routing.py) consumes only the frozen effective record, and the routing record names the frozen values and the source of each (filed or intake-stamped). A post-freeze attempt to supply different risk or surfaces is ignored for routing, recorded as a finding, and fails the run closed at the checks gate with the finding named.
R4: when the order declares a spec_path, the runner hashes every file under that spec's directory at run start; every station's tool permissions deny writes under .openspec/specs/ for the run; the spec-writer verifies the filed spec instead of amending it; the checks gate verifies the filed spec hashes before reviewers launch and fails naming changed paths, spawning no reviewer for that attempt. Orders declaring no spec_path keep today's spec-writer authoring.
R5: the review producer's scoped write pattern generalizes to every station: a station writes only the artifacts its packet names, and never anything under work-orders/, work_orders/, .openspec/specs/, anvil.json or pipelines/. Reviewer stations keep exactly their existing scoped write.
R6: regression tests as new files under tests/: (a) the wo-gh-7 fixture (filed risk medium, surfaces [ui, content, deploy]; intake artifact attempting low and [content]) keeps the filed values, routes the full six reviewer panel of sdlc-default, and records the attempt; (b) intake stamping null fields is accepted, frozen and consumed with sources named; (c) a write attempt to the filed spec path is refused by the wrapper's permission configuration, and the gate hash check passes an untouched tree and fails naming a mutated path; (d) rescope at intake still works with the cut recorded, and a post-freeze description change is refused and recorded.

RECONCILIATION WITH ACTIVE SPECS (read before building; these are decisions, not discoveries for the line to make):
This order deliberately amends two active specs, landed as dated amendment sections in those files in the form the checks-gate loopback rounds used. intake-outcomes: its stamping rule gains the filed-values-win condition and the freeze at intake completion; its rescope discipline (cut recorded, never silent) is unchanged. risk-routing: its trust rule changes from trusting the intake outcomes as authoritative to trusting the frozen effective record; its routing table is unchanged. No other active spec conflicts: the checks gate's protected path rule judges the builder's delta after the fact, while R1 and R4 stop the write itself at the tool layer, so the two mechanisms complement rather than duplicate; the review producer spec already establishes the tool-layer scoped write this order generalizes.

BUILDER REPORT REQUIRED LITERALS: the builder report (runs/wo-gh-40/builder.output.md) must contain each of these in full, unabbreviated: 4675a131eb9aa88097741dc3cdc9772c3db17550, filed-order-immutability, frozen effective record, wo-gh-7. It must also state the base ref it verified the tree against, the exact full factory test count from the suite run, and the names of the new test files added.

GUARDRAILS: authorized surface for this order: anvil/runner.py, anvil/routing.py, anvil/model.py, anvil/executor.py, anvil/gates.py, tools/claude_station.py, tools/dispatch_station.py if needed, stations/intake/PROMPT.md (the stamping and freeze contract sentences only), .openspec/specs/intake-outcomes/spec.md and .openspec/specs/risk-routing/spec.md (dated amendment sections only), the factory docs that describe intake stamping or routing trust (docs/EXECUTION.md at minimum), CHANGELOG.md, one new decision record under brain/decisions/, and new test files under tests/. Pipeline files under pipelines/ are protected paths in anvil.json; the fix must hold without editing them. anvil.json itself is protected; do not edit it. Existing test files at the base ref are protected: do not modify or delete them; new tests arrive as new files. Frozen: the review parse contract, the canonical review contract wording, the reviewer prompts and their Output Format sections, the review producer mechanisms, the checks gate's verdicts and loopback accounting. Python standard library only, no new dependency. No em dash or en dash character in any produced file. Nothing in this order merges, publishes or deploys anything; the run stops at the owner human gate.

GitHub issue: https://github.com/arananet/anvil-factory/issues/40
title: Filed order and spec immutability during a run: stations cannot reclassify a filed order or amend its spec, enforced at the tool layer
